stem: An operations lead uses Claude to assist with two separate deliverables: an internal weekly brainstorming summary for team peers, and a formal compliance report for external regulatory auditors. When establishing the quality control and review depth standards for each deliverable, which approach correctly reflects human accountability standards?

options.text: The external filing requires independent human verification of all cited facts, whereas the internal team digest permits lightweight spot-checking.
Both deliverables require identical line-by-line verification by legal counsel before being shared with colleagues or external stakeholders.
The regulatory report can rely on Claude's self-generated verification notes if executed using maximum reasoning effort settings.
The internal digest requires deeper factual verification than the regulatory filing because team members act on preliminary ideas quickly.

explanation: Review depth and verification standards must scale with the risk profile and consequence of error. High-stakes external regulatory filings require rigorous independent human verification, whereas low-stakes internal team digests tolerate lightweight spot-checks.

distractorNotes.identical-legal-verification: Applying identical formal legal verification to informal internal brainstorming digests creates unnecessary operational overhead.
distractorNotes.rely-on-automated-evaluations: High effort levels improve model reasoning but do not eliminate hallucinations or satisfy human accountability requirements for regulatory compliance.
distractorNotes.intensify-internal-draft-review: Review depth scales directly with the severity of error consequences, which are substantially higher for external regulatory filings than internal digests.

sourceNote: Help Center guidance on review depth, accountability, and appropriate artifact sharing
